scope: Theorem 1.4 (Incompatible descent exponents) of the manuscript “Counterexamples to weak chromatic splitting: sphere kernels and descent exponents” (preprints/Counterexamples-to-weak-chromatic-splitting-sphere-kernels-and-descent-exponents-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f646b6facb641430), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every prime p ≥ 5, with m = p2 + 2, expH(Ep−1) > m, expH (︁ T(Bp) )︁ ≤ m. A homotopy retraction of ip,X would make Ep−1 an H-equivariant retract of T(Bp). Hence ip,X has no homotopy retraction, independently of Theorem 1.1.
